title: The integrated likelihood and its approximations
title_html: The integrated likelihood and its approximations
html:
In @def-gmm-glmm write 𝛃𝛉ψi(ui)=log⁡f(yi∣ui;β,ϕ)+log⁡p(ui;θ).

  1. Factorization. If the random effects split into independent blocks u1,…,um with ui entering only the observations of cluster i, then 𝛃𝛉L(β,θ,ϕ)=∏i=1m∫Rq0exp⁡{ψi(ui)}dui,{#eq-gmm-factorized}

    a product of m integrals of dimension q0.

  2. Laplace approximation. Fix i and take q0=1. Let ψi be four times continuously differentiable with a unique interior maximizer u^i, and ci=−ψi″(u^i)>0. Then, formally, ∫eψi(u)du=2πcieψi(u^i){1+δi+…},δi=ψi(4)(u^i)8ci2+5{ψi‴(u^i)}224ci3.{#eq-gmm-laplace}

    Suppose ψi=niki+si, where ki does not depend on ni and has a nondegenerate maximum and si has derivatives bounded uniformly in ni. (In a GLMM niki is the conditional log-likelihood and si the log prior density of ui, which does not grow with ni.) Then both terms of δi are O(ni−1): the Laplace approximation has relative error O(ni−1) and the error in the log-likelihood is O(∑ini−1).

  3. Adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature. Let (zk,wk)k=1K be the nodes and weights of K-point Gauss–Hermite quadrature, so that ∫e−z2P(z)dz=∑kwkP(zk) for every polynomial P of degree at most 2K−1. With σ^i=ci−1/2, the substitution u=u^i+2σ^iz gives the approximation ∫eψi(u)du≈2σ^i∑k=1Kwkezk2eψi(u^i+2σ^izk).{#eq-gmm-aghq}

    It is exact whenever eψi(u^i+2σ^iz)+z2 is a polynomial of degree at most 2K−1 in z, and K=1 reproduces @eq-gmm-laplace without its correction terms.

  4. Penalized quasi-likelihood avoids the integral altogether, by a penalized maximization that is cheaper than either of the above and carries a bias that does not vanish. It is stated and proved separately as @prp-gmm-pql.
